abstract: Efficient energy prediction is essential for maintaining a balance between demand and supply. The accuracy of the prediction process relies significantly on accurate data processing. Within this process, outliers detection stands out as a critical step, ensuring the reliability and precision of energy predictions. This study focuses on the integration of a Multivariate Outliers Detection (MOD) approach within the Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) model for predicting Photovoltaic (PV) power data. Encompassing 31 PV arrays with diverse technologies and structures. Through this investigation, we aim to shed light on the impact of multivariate outliers in predicting the PV power using LSTM model, offering valuable insights for advancing the reliability and explainability of PV power predictions.

articleTitle: Computer Vision serving visually impaired people
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: To explore and recognize 3D objects, various solutions exist, such as the use of 3D glasses and immersive glasses. If these devices are suitable for persons without visual impairment, they still unusable for those with visual impairments. In this work, we propose an alternative device adapted to these people and which is based on the use of a 2D screen. In order to make the recognition of 3D objects possible on ordinary 2D screens, the renderings of 3D objects are augmented by image processing and a suitable interface. This tool, developed under Unity, makes it possible to exploit the wealth of information inherent in 3D models without having to resort to segmentation and voice transcription. The contribution of this article lies in the co-design of the tool with visually impaired people, in the proposal of a tool that can be parameterized and customized according to needs, and in its evaluation in an ecological environment by visually impaired people. The results of this evaluation confirm the value of the tool for optimizing the residual vision of visually impaired people.

articleTitle: MindWave app: Leveraging AI for Mental Health Support in English and Arabic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The global concern regarding mental health, especially amidst crises like stress, burnout or depression, necessitates accessible platforms catering to diverse populations, including Arabic speakers. This paper introduces “MindWave,” a pioneering web application for English and Arabic-speaking communities. It is an innovative web application designed to offer support and early detection for individuals experiencing or at risk of mental health. The app uses advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Sentiment Analysis (SA) to analyze user-generated text to detect signs of mental health, providing personalized insights, resources, and support for users in need. Its innovation lies in seamlessly integrating text and voice to comprehensively assess emotional well-being. The app fosters a supportive community where users can connect, share experiences, and provide mutual support. Users can engage in discussions, join support groups, or share coping strategies in a safe and anonymous environment. To address the absence of Arabic sentiment datasets for mental health, this study explores the effectiveness of fine-tuning various pre-trained Machine Translation (MT) models from English to Arabic using our parallel dataset of 945,383 sentences. Furthermore, the study delves into training different variants of Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) models on two distinct datasets: the original English dataset and the translated Arabic dataset. The classifiers’ performance trained on the source English dataset is juxtaposed with the results achieved when trained on the translated Arabic dataset. Moreover, we conduct a comparative evaluation of diverse tokenization techniques for Arabic, including Stochastic tokenizer, Disjoint-letter tokenizer, and Morphological tokenizer.

articleTitle: A novel MLP-Mixer and channel attention based network for medical image segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is vital for clinical applications, aiding in precise diagnosis and treatment planning. While Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) were traditionally used for image classification, the emergence of the MLP-Mixer architecture has demonstrated their efficacy beyond classification tasks. In this paper, we introduce a novel network architecture that combines the strengths of MLP-Mixer and channel attention mechanisms, specifically tailored for medical image segmentation. Our proposed mixer-block, integrating the MLP-Mixer with a channel attention module, enhances the network’s capability to focus on relevant features and capture intricate details in medical images. By incorporating this mixer-block into the U-Net architecture, we achieve improved segmentation performance. The proposed architecture outperformed State-of-the-Art (SOTA) methods on BUSI dataset achieving a dice coefficient of 81.45%.

articleTitle: Securing IoT Communication: A Steganographic Protocol for Efficient Mutual Authentication and Data Integrity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: In the rapidly expanding domain of the Internet of Things (IoT), securing communication channels is paramount. This paper introduces a novel protocol that efficiently ensures mutual authentication and data integrity with minimal resource expenditure. Unlike traditional methods, which often require multiple message exchanges and computationally intensive cryptographic operations, our protocol achieves both objectives within only two exchanges. Leveraging steganography and non-cryptographic hash functions, the protocol embeds authentication data within the data payload itself, thus obviating the need for separate authentication phases and significantly reducing the system’s vulnerability to common cyber threats such as Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) and replay attacks. Our approach employs a dual-functionality strategy that simultaneously verifies data integrity during the authentication process, enhancing the security of IoT communications. A comparative analysis with existing solutions, highlights our protocol’s superior efficiency and lower operational costs. The use of indexed, non-repetitive key pairs and steganographic concealment ensures that security does not come at the expense of performance, making the protocol particularly suitable for resource-constrained IoT devices. This paper’s results indicate that our protocol not only meets the stringent security demands of IoT ecosystems but does so while respecting the critical need for energy and computational efficiency. By streamlining the number of message exchanges and employing low-cost hash functions, the protocol sets a new standard for secure IoT communications, paving the way for its widespread adoption in next-generation IoT applications.

articleTitle: Recommendation system for E-learners: model-based collaborative filtering approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: The e-learning recommendation systems help learners in making choices based on their personal preferences, even if they don’t have enough experience to compare different alternatives. Implementing a recommendation system in an online learning environment, that provides learners with several choices based on their personal experience. In this article, an intelligent adaptive e-learning system has been proposed, combining machine learning and reinforcement learning. This system aims to offer an individualized learning path to a specific learner to recommend an adaptive learning path, by applying the Collaborative Filtering algorithm based on SVD and data mining. The proposed system is broken down into three main modules, the data pre-processing module, the model creation module based on learner preferences, and the learning path recommendation module. The interactions between these three modules allow a personalized adaptation according to the preferences of the learner. Furthermore, we conducted some experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of our contribution. The proposed strategy demonstrated that by taking into account the learner’s personal preferences, the student’s learning experience can be improved and strengthened during the learning activity.

articleTitle: Precision Agriculture Deep Neural Network Driven Multi-hop Plant Image Noisy Data Transmission and Plant Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Under precision agriculture (PA), plant disease detection (PDD) is imperative regarding farm crops’ life quality and crop yield. However, the data captures for PDD is influenced by the noisy data captured by farm sensors due to wireless noisy transmission channels. Hence, this work considers the onsite or offsite (remote) farm PDD through onsite farm monitoring PA sensor networks (PAN). Here, effects on captured sensor image (plant leaf image) data transmitted through the PAN to an PDD application are studied. Where both traditional decodeand-forward (DF) data routing and channel-effect considering machine learning data autoencoder routing are used for image data transmission. In addition, a PDD deep learning algorithm is developed to predict whether or not a farm plant is diseased, based on the noisy image data captured by the PAN through data routing. From the PAN-PDD simulation, the proposed ML PANPDD algorithm showed fair performance over the DF PAN-PDD.

articleTitle: Multi-features learning via Attention-BLSTM for Speech Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Within the domain of human-computer interaction, Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has assumed critical importance, where the careful selection of feature representation stands as a key determinant. This study is driven by the objective of conducting a comprehensive comparative analysis through the implementation of a parallel multi-feature design, strategically aimed to effectively characterize the emotional information within speech signals. The innovation of our proposed approach lies in the integration of frameworks, including ImageBind, WavLM, HuBERT, Wav2vec 2-xlsr, along with the commonly used MFCC features. Leveraging their knowledge and adaptability, we tailor these frameworks to meet the specific demands of SER task. Furthermore, to encompass a rich set of multi-features, we introduced an Attention-based Bidirectional Long ShortTerm Memory (attention-BLSTM) network to capture and learn the distinct emotional speech representations extracted through various methods. The experimental evaluations were executed using the IEMOCAP database, and the most remarkable results were attained by employing ImageBind embeddings with our proposed attention-BLSTM, achieving an accuracy of $81.03 \%$. This outcome outshines the current state-of-the-art approaches in SER.

articleTitle: Speech as a Window to the Brain: Innovative Techniques in Early Alzheimer’s Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: As dementia cases are projected to reach 150 million by 2050, with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) accounting for $60-70 \%$ of instances, early detection becomes crucial. AD and other dementias currently rank as the seventh leading cause of death globally. Our study addresses this by employing speech analysis for AD detection, offering a non-invasive and cost-effective diagnostic tool. Utilizing the ADReSS dataset, we integrated advanced Deep Learning techniques, including YAMNet and VGGish, with Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) for feature extraction. An autoencoder was employed for dimensionality reduction to isolate key speech features. We applied Random Forest (RF), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for classification. The ANN model outperformed others, achieving an impressive $89.3 \%$ accuracy, surpassing current methodologies. This research highlights the efficacy of using speech analysis and ML, DL for early AD detection. Our approach, accessible and precise, promises advancements in early diagnosis and care for AD. Future work will aim to enhance model applicability to various stages of AD and related disorders.

articleTitle: Novel approach for detecting Bacterial spot combining Transfer Learning and Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Signal, Image, Video and Communications (ISIVC)
abstract: Bacterial spot, a pervasive disease affecting Solanaceae crops such as tomatoes and peppers, poses a significant threat to global food security and agricultural productivity. This paper presents a novel approach that integrates transfer learning techniques with Large Language Models (LLMs) to detect bacterial spot with high accuracy and efficiency. We employed state-of-the-art convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, including Inception-V3 and MobileNet-V2, which were pre-trained on extensive image datasets and fine-tuned on a curated dataset comprising both PlantVillage images and in-house generated photographs from diverse agricultural settings. These images were further enhanced for model training through age and color classification, addressing the phenotypic variability inherent in real-world agricultural environments.The performance of the CNN models was rigorously evaluated, with Inception-V3 achieving a remarkable 97% accuracy in identifying bacterial spot, while the integration with LLMs provided critical insights into disease management strategies, effectively creating a multifaceted decision support system. The LLMs facilitated the interpretation of complex disease symptoms and treatment efficacy reports, enhancing the overall precision of the diagnostic process.Our research underscores the potential of combining transfer learning and LLMs to revolutionize plant disease detection and agricultural practices. This integrative approach not only advances the field of precision agriculture but also opens up new pathways for scalable, data-driven solutions to combat plant diseases and bolster crop health monitoring worldwide.
